## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Side

160

- [ReferencedFilesPanel](./index.md#referenced-files-panel)
- [UnderstandingPanel](./index.md#understanding-panel)

## Sidebar

It runs along the right of what it sits beside, with a thin line down its left edge, where the two meet. It is resized by dragging that edge: it starts 260 pixels wide and can't be dragged narrower than 160.
It holds its panels one above the other, in the order it lists them, each across its full width. A single thin line, in the theme's line colour, lies between one panel and the next, never two, unless the next panel says its own change of colour is the edge. A panel that isn't shown for the moment takes no room and leaves no line.
It is on the theme's base surface, as its panels' bodies are.

## Concept

### Pitch

A second [SidebarScope](../sidebar/index.md#sidebar-scope), at the right of the message list, that lists the spec files the running task references, so it's clear what part of the spec the harness is working from, and the constraints it has taken from it for the task.

### Shape

#### Description

It runs the full height of the message list, above the chat input, which stays across the full width of prompt mode. It keeps the width it was dragged to while the application runs.
Its two panels, the referenced files above the understanding, sit one above the other: the referenced files only as tall as their rows need, up to half the sidebar's height, scrolling beyond that, and the understanding filling the rest.

#### Look

The sidebar's body is on the ribbon's command area colour, #222222 in dark mode. Each panel's header is 32 pixels tall, on the darkest surface, #111111 in dark mode, as the file tree is, its title in small semibold text, 8 pixels from the left, with no count beside it. There is no line anywhere in it, not between a header and its body, nor between one panel and the next: the change of colour is the edge. The only line is the one down its left edge, where it meets the message list, which is the handle it is resized by. In light mode the same steps are taken, as the ribbon's are.
Neither panel has a permanent scrollbar, since its column would break the 8 pixel inset: a panel shows its scrollbar only while its contents are taller than it, and none otherwise. When it shows, it is the same scrollbar as every other, as the [ScrollbarScope](../scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope) says.

It is only there while a task is running: from the moment a task is sent from the Code, Chain, or Spec tab until its run is over. Questions from the Ask tab never show it, even when one is sent from the queue.
When a task starts, it slides out from the message list's right edge, growing from nothing to its width, its contents sliding into view from behind that edge as it does. When the run is over, it slides back the same way. The slide is quick and settles without bouncing. The message list takes the rest of the width, laid out anew only once the slide settles, as when a file's split opens.

# Scrollbar Scope

## How To Build

A ScrollbarScope should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A ScrollbarScope should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Concept

### Pitch

A permanent scrollbar for any list that scrolls, laid out as a narrow column of its own beside the list rather than over it.

### Shape

#### Description

A narrow column along the right of the list, always shown, whether or not the list has anything to scroll. It is the list's only scrollbar: no scrollbar is laid over the list, or appears only while hovering or scrolling.

#### Surface

Every scrollbar is this one, wherever it is. It has no background of its own: the column takes the colour of the surface it sits on, so on the file tree it is the tree's colour, and on a panel's body the body's. Nothing in it is a colour of its own; the track, the thumb's ends, the arrows, and the thumb's lightening are all black or white laid over that surface, so the scrollbar looks the same on any of them.
The strengths given here are dark mode's. Light mode takes the same steps, gentler: the track is black laid a fifth of the way over the surface, the thumb's ends a tenth, and the thumb lightens with white laid about a fifth of the way while hovered and about a third while dragged. Its arrows are darker than the surface rather than lighter, black laid about a third of the way over it, since white would all but vanish on a light surface.

#### Buttons

A square button at the top of the column scrolls the list up a little, and a square button at the bottom scrolls it down a little. The column is 18 pixels wide, and each button is 17 pixels tall, as wide as the column. A button shows only a small solid arrow, pointing up or down, 6 pixels wide and 4 tall, centred across it, 7 pixels from its top pointing up and from its bottom pointing down, drawn crisp on whole pixels rather than smoothed, in a faint grey, #4d4d4d on #222222 in dark mode, white laid about a fifth of the way over the surface; it has no background, border, or line of its own until the pointer is over it, when it has the bevel of the [ThemeScope](../../theme/index.md#theme-scope), and while pressed with the pointer still over it, its pressed bevel instead. Neither bevel takes the mouse.

#### Track

Between the buttons runs the track, from just beneath the top button to just above the bottom one, inset one pixel from either side of the column, so a pixel of the surface shows down both its sides. The track is dark, black laid half way over the surface, #111111 on #222222 in dark mode, and no line runs beside it or around it. The column has no border at all, against the list or anywhere else.
The track holds a thumb as tall as the share of the list in view, and never too short to grab, placed as far down the track as the list is scrolled. The thumb is a plain rectangle, as wide as the column, covering the track's inset, with no rounded corners, no border, no bevel, and no background of its own: it is the surface's colour, so it reads as a gap of the surface in the dark track. Its top and bottom ends each have a single pixel between the track's colour and the surface's, black laid a quarter of the way over the surface, #191919 on #222222 in dark mode, softening where the track meets it. It lightens a step while the pointer is over it, as white laid over it, and another step while it is being dragged, white laid about 3.5% and 7% of the way over it in dark mode, and goes back as soon as neither is true. Nothing in the column lightens while something else, like a sidebar's edge, is being dragged across it. With nothing to scroll, the thumb fills the track.
Pressing the thumb and dragging scrolls the list with it for as long as the button is held, even once the pointer leaves the column, and pressing the track elsewhere moves the thumb there, from where it can be dragged straight away. Where a resize edge beside the list overlaps the column, a press goes to whichever of the two has the smaller hit area, as the main window says.

#### Steadiness

The thumb never jumps. Its size and place always reflect the whole list's real height, including a list that only draws the rows in view: every row is measured, even those never scrolled into view, so the thumb doesn't grow, shrink, or leap as rows come into view. A row that arrives, or changes, while out of view counts at its height as soon as it does, and after the list's width changes, rewrapping its rows, the height is known in full again by the next frame. Only what has changed is measured again, so a long list stays as quick to scroll and to add to as one that measures only what is in view; only a change of width measures every row again.
A row's height is the same measured out of view as drawn in it. Text in a row, such as a reply's markdown, is parsed once and kept for as long as the app runs, not only while its row is drawn, so a row scrolled away and back is never parsed again, nor shorter for a moment while it is. Long text is parsed in the background, so a row holding it may first measure short: while it parses, its row is measured again every fraction of a second, for a few seconds at most, so the height is right as soon as the parse lands, whether or not the row is in view. Dragging the thumb, it stays under the pointer the whole way, rows coming into view or not.

#### Lock To Bottom

A list that keeps receiving output, like a task's, adds one more square button, drawn as the others are, below the others, with a pixel of the surface between it and the down button, that locks the scroll to the bottom. Its arrow is the down arrow with a short bar beneath it, the same 6 pixels wide. While it is locked, the button shows as selected, with the pressed bevel of the [ThemeScope](../../theme/index.md#theme-scope) whether or not the pointer is over it, and the list stays scrolled to the bottom as output arrives. Pressing it again unlocks it. Its tooltip says which it will do.

##### Lock Pulse

Whenever the scroll becomes locked, whether by pressing the button or by scrolling to the bottom by hand, a glowing pulse emanates from the lock button once, to confirm it. It is a single, brief confirmation in the manner of Apple's own, not a repeating pulse, which would suggest something still going on.
The pulse is in the theme's focus ring colour. A soft, blurred glow blooms around the button, quickly, and fades away. At the same time two thin rings ripple out from the button's centre, the second a moment after the first, each starting as a circle the size of the button and growing to nearly three times that, easing out so it slows as it spreads, thinning and fading to nothing as it goes. All of it is over in under a second. It is drawn over whatever is beside the column, but never takes the mouse.
A list that shows already locked doesn't pulse, and unlocking the scroll while it pulses stops the pulse straight away.

Scrolling the list by hand locks and unlocks it as well: scrolling with the mouse wheel or trackpad over the list, pressing the column's up or down button, or pressing or dragging its thumb. Scrolled by hand to the bottom, the scroll locks there, just as if the button had been pressed. Scrolled by hand away from the bottom while it is locked, the lock breaks straight away, leaving the list wherever it was scrolled to. A list with nothing to scroll keeps its lock as it is. The button stays the way to lock or unlock it wherever the list is: pressing it to lock scrolls the list to the bottom, and pressing it to unlock leaves the list unlocked until it is next scrolled to the bottom by hand.

Nothing in it is a colour of its own; the track, the thumb's ends, the arrows, and the thumb's lightening are all black or white laid over that surface, so the scrollbar looks the same on any of them.
The strengths given here are dark mode's. Light mode takes the same steps, gentler: the track is black laid a fifth of the way over the surface, the thumb's ends a tenth, and the thumb lightens with white laid about a fifth of the way while hovered and about a third while dragged. Its arrows are darker than the surface rather than lighter, black laid about a third of the way over it, since white would all but vanish on a light surface.

#### Buttons

A square button at the top of the column scrolls the list up a little, and a square button at the bottom scrolls it down a little. The column is 18 pixels wide, and each button is 17 pixels tall, as wide as the column. A button shows only a small solid arrow, pointing up or down, 6 pixels wide and 4 tall, centred across it, 7 pixels from its top pointing up and from its bottom pointing down, drawn crisp on whole pixels rather than smoothed, in a faint grey, #4d4d4d on #222222 in dark mode, white laid about a fifth of the way over the surface; it has no background, border, or line of its own until the pointer is over it, when it has the bevel of the [ThemeScope](../../theme/index.md#theme-scope), and while pressed with the pointer still over it, its pressed bevel instead. Neither bevel takes the mouse.

#### Track

Between the buttons runs the track, from just beneath the top button to just above the bottom one, inset one pixel from either side of the column, so a pixel of the surface shows down both its sides. The track is dark, black laid half way over the surface, #111111 on #222222 in dark mode, and no line runs beside it or around it. The column has no border at all, against the list or anywhere else.
The track holds a thumb as tall as the share of the list in view, and never too short to grab, placed as far down the track as the list is scrolled. The thumb is a plain rectangle, as wide as the column, covering the track's inset, with no rounded corners, no border, no bevel, and no background of its own: it is the surface's colour, so it reads as a gap of the surface in the dark track. Its top and bottom ends each have a single pixel between the track's colour and the surface's, black laid a quarter of the way over the surface, #191919 on #222222 in dark mode, softening where the track meets it. It lightens a step while the pointer is over it, as white laid over it, and another step while it is being dragged, white laid about 3.5% and 7% of the way over it in dark mode, and goes back as soon as neither is true. Nothing in the column lightens while something else, like a sidebar's edge, is being dragged across it. With nothing to scroll, the thumb fills the track.
Pressing the thumb and dragging scrolls the list with it for as long as the button is held, even once the pointer leaves the column, and pressing the track elsewhere moves the thumb there, from where it can be dragged straight away. Where a resize edge beside the list overlaps the column, a press goes to whichever of the two has the smaller hit area, as the main window says.

#### Steadiness

The thumb never jumps. Its size and place always reflect the whole list's real height, including a list that only draws the rows in view: every row is measured, even those never scrolled into view, so the thumb doesn't grow, shrink, or leap as rows come into view. A row that arrives, or changes, while out of view counts at its height as soon as it does, and after the list's width changes, rewrapping its rows, the height is known in full again by the next frame. Only what has changed is measured again, so a long list stays as quick to scroll and to add to as one that measures only what is in view; only a change of width measures every row again.
A row's height is the same measured out of view as drawn in it. Text in a row, such as a reply's markdown, is parsed once and kept for as long as the app runs, not only while its row is drawn, so a row scrolled away and back is never parsed again, nor shorter for a moment while it is. Long text is parsed in the background, so a row holding it may first measure short: while it parses, its row is measured again every fraction of a second, for a few seconds at most, so the height is right as soon as the parse lands, whether or not the row is in view. Dragging the thumb, it stays under the pointer the whole way, rows coming into view or not.

#### Lock To Bottom

A list that keeps receiving output, like a task's, adds one more square button, drawn as the others are, below the others, with a pixel of the surface between it and the down button, that locks the scroll to the bottom. Its arrow is the down arrow with a short bar beneath it, the same 6 pixels wide. While it is locked, the button shows as selected, with the pressed bevel of the [ThemeScope](../../theme/index.md#theme-scope) whether or not the pointer is over it, and the list stays scrolled to the bottom as output arrives. Pressing it again unlocks it. Its tooltip says which it will do.

##### Lock Pulse

Whenever the scroll becomes locked, whether by pressing the button or by scrolling to the bottom by hand, a glowing pulse emanates from the lock button once, to confirm it. It is a single, brief confirmation in the manner of Apple's own, not a repeating pulse, which would suggest something still going on.
The pulse is in the theme's focus ring colour. A soft, blurred glow blooms around the button, quickly, and fades away. At the same time two thin rings ripple out from the button's centre, the second a moment after the first, each starting as a circle the size of the button and growing to nearly three times that, easing out so it slows as it spreads, thinning and fading to nothing as it goes. All of it is over in under a second. It is drawn over whatever is beside the column, but never takes the mouse.
A list that shows already locked doesn't pulse, and unlocking the scroll while it pulses stops the pulse straight away.

Scrolling the list by hand locks and unlocks it as well: scrolling with the mouse wheel or trackpad over the list, pressing the column's up or down button, or pressing or dragging its thumb. Scrolled by hand to the bottom, the scroll locks there, just as if the button had been pressed. Scrolled by hand away from the bottom while it is locked, the lock breaks straight away, leaving the list wherever it was scrolled to. A list with nothing to scroll keeps its lock as it is. The button stays the way to lock or unlock it wherever the list is: pressing it to lock scrolls the list to the bottom, and pressing it to unlock leaves the list unlocked until it is next scrolled to the bottom by hand.

I fixed a case where the understanding panel scrolled when nothing overflowed. I couldn't reproduce the "couple of pixels" scroll you saw, so I'm not sure these changes cover it.

**What I found:** the rendering tests measure exactly 0px of scroll room in both panels whenever their rows fit. That held at scale factors 1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75 and 2, and at odd and fractional window sizes. The one case that did scroll was when the understanding file existed but had no list items yet, for example just after the harness creates it. The list then had no children, and gpui counts an empty list's whole box plus its 8px padding as content, so the panel scrolled by 16px. It would also have shown its scrollbar.

**Changes in `src/referenced_spec.rs`:**
- **Empty understanding:** the list now gets an invisible child when the file exists but has no items, so there's nothing to scroll. This is the part I found and fixed.
- **Rounding margin:** a panel now counts as overflowing only when it's at least 1px taller than its space. When it doesn't overflow, its scroll position is held at 0, so tiny rounding leftovers can't scroll it. This is my guess at what you saw, but it only covers up to 1px. If the scroll you saw is 2–3px, the cause is still unknown.

**Tests:** I added checks to `referenced_spec_takes_the_mockups_look` that neither panel scrolls when its rows fit, and that an understanding with no list items has no scroll room and no scrollbar. The new check fails without the fix and passes with it. The full suite has 3 failures that also fail without my changes: `batch_sent_tasks_run_in_order_in_the_other_mode`, `selected_answer_text_can_be_copied_or_attached` and `defaults_are_this_repositorys_templates`. A fourth, `raw_prompt_opens_once_the_task_has_compiled`, failed once in the full run and passed on 3 separate runs, so it looks flaky rather than broken by this.

The spec itself contradicts on this point. The sidebar's Look section says a panel shows its scrollbar only when its contents overflow. Each panel's own section says "a permanent scrollbar along its right". The code follows the Look section, which matches what you asked for.
